name: AgentEvolver: Towards Efficient Self-Evolving Agent System
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2511.10395 [cs.LG]); not peer-reviewed at time of writing (technical report from Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
authors_affiliation: Yunpeng Zhai, Shuchang Tao, Cheng Chen, Anni Zou, Ziqian Chen, Qingxu Fu, Shinji Mai, Li Yu, Jiaji Deng, Zouying Cao, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou. Affiliation: Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group.
code_url: https://github.com/modelscope/AgentEvolver (Apache-2.0). Experience management implemented via ReMe: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/modelscope/AgentEvolver (actively maintained; homepage https://modelscope.github.io/AgentEvolver/; follow-up releases SeeUPO and CuES tracked in README)
task_domain: tool-use / decision-making (long-horizon, tool-augmented LLM agents trained with RL); evaluated on tool/API-calling agent benchmarks
problem_setting: Interactive, online RL setting for LLM-based agents in tool-augmented multi-turn environments. The agent operates in an 'interaction sandbox' E=(S,A,P) that provides state/action/transition dynamics but no reward function and no predefined task distribution. The agent must autonomously synthesize its own training tasks (proxy task distribution p_train approximating an unknown target distribution p_target) and reward signals, then optimize a goal-conditioned policy via GRPO-style RL. Single-agent (one policy network); supervision (oracle reward/task labels) is NOT assumed at training time — tasks and rewards are self-generated, with an LLM judge providing synthetic rewards. Backbone: Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct.
what_is_retrieved: experiences — distilled natural-language units of structured knowledge (skills/tactics/precautions and failure notes) derived from past successful and unsuccessful trajectories, each formatted as {When to use, Content}. Used as in-context guidance during rollout.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes: an experience pool P_exp constructed offline from the policy's own rollouts on self-generated tasks (cold-start pool construction) and queried online during rollout. The store is induced from the agent's own trajectories rather than a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking: experience retrieval selects the TopK (k=5) experiences by cosine similarity, followed by a rerank-and-rewrite refinement. No notion of minimal-set completeness or precision-driven variable-size recommendation is reported.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (yes: cosine top-k retrieval of experiences by query), Reuse (yes: retrieved experience injected into prompt for in-context guidance during rollout), Revise (partial: a re-ranking + re-writing refinement module Omega_refine rewrites retrieved experiences for generality; experiences are distilled/validated rather than per-case adapted to the new problem), Retain (yes: validated experiences indexed into the vector store / experience pool). Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=partial, Retain=yes]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It realizes CBR-like mechanisms (experience acquisition, retrieval, reuse via ICL, retention) under the terminology of 'self-navigating', 'experience reuse', and 'experience pool'.
retrieval_unit: experience = a distilled natural-language guideline/insight unit comprising a 'When to use' applicability condition (used as the retrieval key) and a 'Content' body (instructions, precautions, recommended strategies). Conceptually a strategy/guideline distilled from trajectories rather than a raw trajectory; effectively a case-like (condition -> guidance) unit.
index_source: Hybrid construction: offline-induced cold-start experience pool P_exp built from N_pc=4 rollouts per self-generated task by the initial policy, processed (preprocess -> extract -> validate -> index) into a vector store; queried online at rollout/inference time. Induced from the agent's own experiences (not a static external corpus).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: experiences encoded as embeddings (of the 'When to use' field) in a vector store; retrieval by cosine similarity over flat embeddings (implemented via ReMe). No graph or explicit hierarchy reported.
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based cosine similarity retrieval), followed by an LLM-based re-ranking and re-writing refinement stage.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf) for the retriever itself: retrieval uses fixed embedding cosine similarity (top-k); the retriever is not trained with task-effectiveness, contrastive, or RL signals. (Note: the upstream experience extraction/validation uses an LLM evaluator, but the similarity retriever is off-the-shelf.)
query_construction: From a task g, an associated query q is extracted and encoded into an embedding h_q; this is matched against experience embeddings h_e (the experiences' 'When to use' fields). Raw task/query embedding; no decomposition or synthetic query expansion reported for the retrieval query.
query_granularity: task-level: the query is constructed per task (one-shot at the start of a rollout), and the retrieved experience is injected into the initial prompt of the rollout. Not per-step.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: experience is retrieved once per task at the start of an experience-guided rollout and injected into the initial prompt; not iterative or uncertainty-triggered within a trajectory.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / proportion-controlled: a fixed fraction eta=0.5 of rollouts within each query group are designated experience-guided (N_e = floor(eta*N)); for those rollouts a relevant experience is retrieved and injected. Retrieval is triggered by the rollout-mixing schedule rather than by token confidence, uncertainty, or an agent-initiated request.
reranking: Yes: a refinement module Omega_refine performs (1) re-ranking of the top-k retrieved experiences to ensure contextual relevance and task alignment, and (2) re-writing to improve generality/adaptability. (LLM-based refinement; not a classical cross-encoder.)
retrieved_context_refinement: rerank + re-write (rewrite-for-generality). After cosine top-k, Omega_refine re-ranks for contextual relevance/task alignment and re-writes the retrieved experiences to enhance generality and adaptability before injection.
tool_document_engineering: N/A — retrieved units are experiences (distilled trajectory insights), not tool/skill descriptions; the work does not index tool docstrings for tool retrieval.
index_content_separation: Partial: the 'When to use' field serves as a lightweight retrieval key/condition (vectorized) while the 'Content' field carries the heavier detailed guidance loaded on use. This is a key-then-content split within each experience rather than a separate index-vs-content store.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A — no tool index or external tool integration protocol (RapidAPI/MCP/RESTful) is the retrieval target. Environments are served via a Gym-compatible Environment Service over HTTP; tool/API calls are part of the environment, not a retrieved/synchronized tool store.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A — retrieval does not model inter-tool dependencies; the retrieved units are experiences, not tools.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation via in-context learning (explicit experience): a retrieved experience exp_g is injected into the initial prompt following a template {system_prompt}<EXP>{exp_g}</EXP>{query} to steer the experience-guided rollout. Additionally, used as an implicit training signal — RL training (with experience stripping) makes the policy internalize the experience-induced behavior so that retrieval is NOT needed at final inference.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-act at rollout time (one-shot exemplar/guidance at the start of a trajectory): retrieved experience guides the experience-mixed rollout; combined with an experience-mixed exploration strategy (eta=0.5 vanilla vs experience-guided rollouts) feeding GRPO-style policy optimization. No explicit planner / MCTS / tree search; integration is into the RL rollout-and-update loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-rollout: a single retrieval+injection occurs at the start of each experience-guided rollout (task-level), not interleaved per CoT-step or per tool-call. (Credit assignment, separately, is step-wise.)
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation at the store level: retrieved experiences are re-ranked and re-written (Omega_refine) for generality before use; they are then used as verbatim in-context guidance within the rollout. There is no execution-feedback-driven per-case revision of a single retrieved case; instead RL 'implicit learning' (experience stripping + selective boosting) internalizes the experience.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/guideline in free-text natural language (structured note with 'When to use' + 'Content' fields), injected as plain text in the prompt. Not raw trajectories, not executable programs, not latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy / state-aware guideline-rule: structured natural-language insights ('When to use' applicability condition + 'Content' advice) extracted from successful, failed, or comparative trajectory pairs — higher abstraction than a raw trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Multiple: (1) LLM-based experience validation during pool construction (Omega_process) filters low-quality/unreliable experiences; (2) re-ranking + re-writing refinement (Omega_refine) improves relevance; (3) experience-mixed rollout (eta=0.5) limits over-reliance on retrieved cues; (4) experience stripping removes injected experience tokens before policy-gradient computation so reward is attributed to the model's own reasoning, not to memorized external context; (5) selective boosting handles the off-policy distribution shift from experience-conditioned rollouts.
memory_type: episodic / experience-library (an 'experience pool' of distilled natural-language insights with skill/tactic and failure-note content); stored in a vector store (ReMe).
write_back: Yes. Validated experiences distilled from rollout trajectories are extracted, LLM-validated, and indexed into the long-term experience vector store for subsequent retrieval (Omega_process step 4: vector store updating).
online_growth: Primarily offline-induced cold-start pool with online retrieval. The pool P_exp is constructed from the initial policy's rollouts on self-generated tasks; the paper describes both offline (pool construction) and online (retrieval) phases. Continual online expansion of the pool during deployment is implied by the framework/ReMe but the reported experiments use a cold-start pool built before training; thus growth-during-deployment is [uncertain].
write_back_trigger: on-success-and-failure (reflective, validated): experiences are distilled from successful, failed, AND comparative success/failure trajectory pairs, then passed through an LLM-based experience-validation step before being written. Writes are gated by quality/reliability validation rather than success-only.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure: experiences are distilled from successful, unsuccessful, and comparative (success-vs-failure) trajectory pairs. Failed cases yield corrective insights (e.g., the AppWorld example: 'always verify an API's existence/behavior via apis.api_docs.show_api_doc before executing critical actions'). Both positive and negative experiences inform the 'Content' guidance.
memory_evolution_update: append-and-refine: validated experiences are indexed (append) into the vector store; at retrieval time experiences are re-ranked and re-written for generality (refine). No explicit dedup-merge / forget-prune / link-and-evolve dynamics over stored entries are reported (rewrite happens on retrieval copies, not necessarily overwriting the store). [uncertain] whether stored entries are mutated in place.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case/experience selection is a fixed cosine-similarity top-k (k=5) with LLM re-ranking, not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. (The agent's action policy is RL-trained, but the retriever is not.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory in the reported experiments (one policy's experience pool). The experience pool aggregates the agent's own cross-task experiences but is not shared across heterogeneous agents/frameworks. (Multi-agent co-evolution is listed only as future work.)
benchmarks: AppWorld; BFCL v3 (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard v3, multi-turn split only).
benchmark_family: tool / tool-augmented long-horizon agent benchmarks (AppWorld = app/API task completion; BFCL v3 = multi-turn function-calling). Both are tool/API-use benchmarks under sparse terminal rewards.
baselines: Vanilla GRPO (standard sparse outcome-only RL, deepseek_math GRPO) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct backbones (zero-shot/Backbone also reported). Internal ablation baselines include: training on Original p_target data vs Synthetic p_train vs Hybrid; Navigating w/o selective boosting; Self-Attributing w/o r_attr and w/o r_out; LLM judge w/o principle / w/o reference solution.
key_metrics: Task Goal Completion (TGC) reported as avg@8 (mean TGC over 8 rollouts) and best@8 (best of 8); also avg@4/best@4 in some ablations. Efficiency metrics: Steps@.9 (steps to reach 90% of baseline best), Area Under Curve (AUC) of learning curves.
headline_result: Integrating all three mechanisms (AgentEvolver overall) on Qwen2.5-14B yields overall avg@8 of 57.6% (vs 29.8% backbone), i.e. +27.8% (AppWorld 48.7%, BFCL v3 66.5%), and best@8 73.1% (+30.3%). On Qwen2.5-7B, overall avg@8 improves +29.4% (15.8% -> 45.2%) and best@8 +36.1% (24.0% -> 60.1%).
ablations: Extensive. Main table is itself ablative (Backbone -> +Questioning -> +Questioning&Navigating -> +Questioning&Attributing -> overall), showing self-questioning gives the largest single gain (7B 15.8%->36.1% avg@8). Self-questioning: synthetic p_train approaches human-curated p_target; hybrid p_hybrid surpasses original data; data-volume study (40.3% with 100 samples, diminishing returns at 200/500); cross-domain generalization (14B AppWorld->BFCL drops only 4.3%); LLM-judge ablation shows principle + reference solution are essential. Self-navigating: experience injection at inference +5.4% avg@4 / +6.7% best@4; implicit (RL-internalized) learning beats ICL-only (+34.2% avg@4) and vanilla RL (+7.9% avg@4); removing selective boosting drops below RL baseline (-0.5% avg@4, -2.9% best@4); eta=0.5 best exploration/exploitation balance; eps_hat_high=0.6 best short/long-term balance. Self-attributing: both r_attr and r_out channels needed (w/o r_out worse than w/o r_attr); alpha in [0.10,0.20] optimal; sample efficiency: reaches 90% of baseline best in 40 steps (AppWorld, baseline 90) and 20 steps (BFCL, baseline 60), 55%/67% reductions, higher AUC (46.26 vs 41.03 AppWorld; 61.02 vs 55.78 BFCL).
evaluation_decoupling: No. The work does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) separately. Experience retrieval is evaluated only through its downstream effect on task TGC and trajectory reward, not via standalone retrieval-quality metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed. Final task TGC (outcome) is the primary metric, but the self-attributing mechanism explicitly introduces step-wise process-quality signals (LLM GOOD/BAD attribution per action) and the analysis discusses process correctness vs outcome effectiveness as two reward channels. Reported scores are outcome-oriented (TGC), while process quality is leveraged as a reward/credit-assignment signal rather than as a separately reported evaluation metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency emphasis. Sample efficiency: self-attributing reaches 90% of baseline best performance in 40 vs 90 steps (AppWorld, -55%) and 20 vs 60 steps (BFCL, -67%), with higher AUC. Self-questioning reduces data-construction cost (40.3% with only 100 synthetic samples; synthetic data matches human-curated). Self-navigating improves exploration efficiency / reduces redundant rollouts. Compute: 8x NVIDIA A100 (80GB), built on PyTorch + veRL; lr 1e-6, batch 32, 40 epochs/update, KL coef 0.001, trajectories truncated at 30 steps. Exact API/$ cost of LLM judges (Qwen-Plus/Qwen-Max/Qwen3-235B-A22B) not quantified [uncertain].
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: TopK k=5 experiences retrieved, then re-ranked/re-written; experience-guided rollout fraction eta=0.5; trajectories truncated at a maximum of 30 steps. Explicit token budget for the injected experience block is not reported [uncertain]; selection is fixed-k rather than adaptive/budget-capped.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A — this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a contributed benchmark, but note the self-questioning module synthesizes its own training tasks (LLM-synthesized via curiosity-guided exploration with environment profiles, e.g. queries with two entities/three attributes/three operations at 'hard' difficulty), filtered (lexical dedup threshold 0.8, real-time + post-generation filtering) and scored by an LLM judge (Qwen3-235B-A22B) with reference-solution-based correctness checks; ~100-500 synthetic samples used in volume studies. Evaluation uses existing benchmarks AppWorld and BFCL v3 (multi-turn).
builds_on: GRPO / DeepSeek-Math (deepseek_math) RL objective and simplified advantage estimation (undiscounted cumulative future reward); PPO/GRPO clipping; veRL (HybridFlow, sheng2024hybridflow) distributed RL infrastructure; ReMe (agentscope-ai/ReMe) for experience summarization/management; in-context learning for experience reuse; curiosity-driven / intrinsic-motivation exploration; goal-conditioned RL (universal value functions, schaul2015universal).
contrasts_with: Vanilla GRPO and PPO/GRPO-style agent RL that rely on massive random trajectory sampling and sparse trajectory-level (uniform) credit assignment; handcrafted Process Reward Models (PRMs) with rigid task-specific scoring (contrasted with the LLM GOOD/BAD attribution); workflow-based / human-engineered agent orchestration; RL methods requiring manually constructed task datasets; intrinsic-reward and UCB-bandit exploration strategies that are ineffective for long-horizon tool agents; explicit ICL-only experience use (shown to have a performance ceiling vs implicit RL internalization).
lineage: Decision/Memory + RL lineage (group F_decision_memory_rl): a self-evolving agentic-RL system combining (a) growing experience memory with retrieval-augmented in-context guidance distilled from successful and failed trajectories (skills/tactics/failure notes), and (b) step-level credit assignment via LLM-based attribution, plus self-synthesized tasks. Sits at the intersection of experience-/case-based agent memory and RL-based agent training; positioned as an efficiency-oriented successor to GRPO-style agent RL that internalizes retrieved experience into the policy.
